_comment: Creature progression (D30). All tunable. Move power multiplies existing combat_math damage, so 1.0 preserves today's balance exactly.

level._comment_curve_sh47: SH47/D42 (3-4 hour chapter). EXPONENT WAS 1.6, base was 40. TUNABLE, and the exponent is the single largest lever in this file. Why it moved, measured by tools/_probe_pacing.py against the shipped critical path: with a LINEAR award (`xp_award` below is `base + per_enemy_level * L`) and a cost curve of `base * L^e`, the number of level-matched fights one level costs grows like L^(e-1). At e=1.6 that meant 10.9 fights per level at L5 and 33.7 at L19 -- and the chapter's whole critical path (46 creature battles plus every authored xp_bonus) paid 5104 xp against the 30135 needed to reach the Warden-ready L19. The player made up the other 83% by killing level-2-to-6 wild creatures: 648 of them, 8.1 of the run's 9.0 hours. That is MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md 11's `bad grind` verbatim -- 'walk in circles killing identical weak enemies only to inflate a number' -- and it was the entire overshoot. e=1.15 keeps the one property progression.gd actually requires (each level strictly costs more than the last) and keeps a real sense of slowing (2.4 fights per level at L5, 3.8 at L19) without compounding out of reach. Base stays 40.

_comment_award_sh47: SH47/D42. WAS base 18, per_enemy_level 6, party_share 0.35. ALL TUNABLE. The curve change above is only half the fix: the award also has to keep pace with the enemy levels the chapter actually fields, which run 2 at the practice fight to 22 in the stronghold gauntlet. Doubling both terms (30 + 16L) takes the critical path's own payout from 5104 to 11003 xp against the 10904 the flattened curve asks for the L3 starter to reach the Warden's own level-20 ace -- i.e. the main line alone arrives level with the boss, which tests/test_trainers_data.gd::test_the_critical_path_alone_pays_for_the_warden_ready_level now fails the build over. 16 rather than 15 on the per-level term is exactly that test talking back: at 15 the path paid 10405 against 10904 and landed half a level short. party_share 0.35 -> 0.5 is the quieter half: the bench got barely a third of every fight, so a five that the spec explicitly wants LEVELLED ('level the five' is its first named GOOD grind) fell steadily behind the lead and had to be brought up by repeating fights. At 0.5 ordinary play keeps the team together and the deliberate part of levelling -- choosing who leads, who to bring, who to catch instead -- is what is left.

creature_bed._comment: Gate A owner contract. TUNABLE. A creature in a physical bed heals continuously over ordinary world time and becomes unavailable. full_heal_seconds is the time 0->100% would take if the player never sleeps; sleeping through the night completes any occupied bed immediately and grants the rested state.

_comment_individuality: R4.2, GAME_DESIGN.md 11: 'same-species creatures have slightly different underlying stat quality.' Each core stat (hp/attack/defence) carries its own 0.0-1.0 quality roll, 0.5 = perfectly average -- variance_pct is the swing at the extremes (0.0 or 1.0), so 0.12 means a stat can run +/-12% off the species base. star_thresholds buckets a roll into 1-5 stars for appraisal display (spec: 'show appraisal through stars/bars, not exact IV numbers') -- four cut points splitting 0..1 into five bands.
_comment_traits: R4.2, GAME_DESIGN.md 11: 'each creature starts with one trait. A second trait can develop later through progression/bond.' unlock_bond_nodes reuses bond.thresholds' own node count -- 5 here means every node crossed, the same 'fully bonded' milestone the Team screen already shows.
_comment_evolution: R4.6, spec sec4/D13/D17/D20: keyed by the PRE-evolution species id (species.json's own `evolves_into` names the target, so this block only needs the gate numbers). level/bond gate the live instance; item_id names a catalyst item to consume, empty meaning no item is required. Mudsnout's item_id starts empty ON PURPOSE -- the spec's own suggestion is a Heartstone from the Burrow Warrens (SD17), which does not exist yet, and gating the biome's one evolution on an item nothing can drop would make it unreachable for the whole span between now and Phase 8b. Flip item_id once SD17 ships a real Heartstone pickup; until then this is level+bond only. All numbers (and the item id, once one exists) are tunable per CLAUDE.md -- do not let 15/55 become permanent canon.
_comment_evolution_sd17: SD17 SHIPPED THAT PICKUP, so the flip above has happened: `item_id` is `heartstone` (data/items/items.json), and the one in the world sits in the Burrow Warrens' branch chamber -- past the guardian, off the critical path, one-time. The gate stops being unit-tested-but-off infrastructure and becomes a real reason to clear the dungeon. Still tunable: emptying `item_id` again reverts to level+bond only, with no code change.

elixirs._comment: D47. How many raw stat points one creature may ever gain from elixirs, per stat. The cap is what keeps a permanent booster a prize rather than a grind -- uncapped, coins plus patience convert straight into an arbitrarily strong creature, which is the outcome D37 refused when it kept individuality rolls out of the player's hands. 24 is roughly a handful of levels' worth on a mid-game stat: worth hunting for, never a substitute for levelling. TUNABLE.

_comment_gateb_home: GATEB-FLAGS (68-CHAPTER/17-RG18). What counts as 'a home' for the two building-owned CONTRACT flags data/progression/objectives.json's tournament ladder left unwired -- home_built, home_materials_gathered. Read by scripts/build/home_progress.gd, which explains the reasoning in full; the short version is 'the tutorial camp, enclosed by the smallest room a player would naturally build around it'. required_pieces is the ONE number that decides both flags: home_built is met once GameState.placed_buildings holds at least this many of each id, and home_materials_gathered's threshold is these same pieces' own data/items/buildables.json costs, summed -- never a second hand-typed figure. TUNABLE.
